//: Copy to a machine-local worker.json (never commit it) and point FAMILIAR_WORKER_CONFIG at it.
//token: The Familiar credential is NOT configured here. Set FAMILIAR_RUNNER_TOKEN in the environment.
//capabilities: Roles this worker accepts. An approved step whose role no worker declares stays Started and blocks its task until you capture or cancel it.
//lease: Optional. The worker renews this bounded lease while the adapter runs; expiry recovers crashed work.
//projects: Machine-local repository mapping. Only these projects are ever offered to this worker.

projects.//mode: read-only, or edit-worktree to let approved Implementer sessions change files here. Even then only the Implementer writes; Planner and Reviewer stay read-only. edit-worktree needs a clean LINKED git worktree and refuses to start otherwise. A third mode, local-maintenance, is documented at the end of this file.
projects.//projectPath: Recommended, and required for automatic per-session worktree isolation: the clean canonical checkout used as the current baseline. Each session receives a fresh detached worktree under allowedRoot; without it, only legacy static read-only execution is available.

//host-maintenance: A third mode, local-maintenance, exists for work whose subject is the MACHINE rather than a
repository on it — restarting a unit, reading a disk's health, finding out why a worker stopped.
It grants Bash and runs as this worker's own OS user. See ADR-0021 before using it.
Read this before you copy it: a session in this mode can damage the host. Unlike the other two
modes there is no directory boundary, because a shell has none — allowedRoot '/' is the honest
value, and writing something narrower only misleads the next reader. What bounds it is the OS
user, the single project mapped to it, the Implementer-only role rule, and a human approving the
plan first. Give it its own worker process and its own systemd unit, never a second mapping on
the worker that builds your code, so that stopping one unit is a complete off switch.
A mapping using it looks like this — note that the mode alone does not load, the same mapping
must also acknowledge what it is turning on:
"projectId": "<the project you created for this host>",
"worktree": "/srv/yourapp",        // where the session starts; not a limit on its reach
"acknowledgeHostAccess": true      // required; without it the worker refuses to start
There is deliberately no projectPath: nothing is cloned and no worktree is created.
